steps.title: Have a coffee

smart.title: Smart matching
smart.body: A shared language is required. No repeats with recent matches, a bonus for shared interests, and other teams come first.

rhythm.title: Your rhythm

skip.title: Skip when you’re busy

faq.title: Questions and answers
faq.subtitle: Can’t find your answer? Write to us — we reply to people, not tickets.

items.a: Randomly, with rules. A pair must share a language. We avoid people who met recently, prefer different departments in work workspaces, take the meeting format (in person or online) into account, and give a bonus for shared interests.
On the day and hour your workspace admin chose, in the workspace time zone — for example on the 1st of every month at 9:00. You get an email and see your match on your home screen.
Only what you put in your profile: name, job title, city, format, languages, interests and “ask me about…”. Only people in your workspaces can see your email.
Yes. Workspace settings have “Skip next round” — you’re back in automatically afterwards. Or pause until you switch it back on.

items.q: What if there’s an odd number of people?
items.a: Someone joins a group of three. If someone has no compatible match at all (for example, no shared language), we’ll tell them honestly that there’s no match this time.

items.q: Can I be in several workspaces?
items.a: Yes: work, office, club, friends. Each has its own schedule, and you manage your participation separately.

items.q: How do I keep a workspace to my company?
items.a: When creating it, add allowed email domains, e.g. company.com. The invite link then only works for those addresses; personal invites work for anyone.
We email you a button and a 6-digit code. The code saves the day when a corporate mail filter “checks” the link before you do.
Nakavu is free right now. If paid features for large organisations arrive one day, basic coffee roulette stays free.

items.q: How do I delete my account?
items.a: Account settings → “Delete account”. We remove your profile, match history and memberships in every workspace.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Nakavu collects the minimum needed to introduce people over coffee. We don’t sell data and we don’t show ads.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: Your email address to sign in; the profile you fill in yourself (name, job title, department, city, meeting format, languages, interests, photo); workspace memberships; match history and your “did you meet?” answers.

sections.title: Why
sections.body: To make matches, send match emails and reminders, and show history and (anonymised) statistics to workspace admins.

sections.title: Who sees your data
sections.body: Your profile and email are visible only to members of the workspaces you’re in. Admins see the member list and participation status, but not whether a specific pair met.

sections.title: Where it’s stored
sections.body: In Supabase (database and authentication) in the EU. Emails are sent through Resend. Both process data only on our behalf.

sections.title: How long
sections.body: As long as you have an account. Leaving a workspace deletes your history there; deleting your account deletes everything.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can view and edit your profile any time, turn off emails, leave a workspace or delete your account. Under the GDPR you can also request a copy of your data — just write to us.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body: Only the essentials: your sign-in session, chosen language and theme. No third-party analytics.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By using Nakavu you agree to these simple rules.

sections.title: The service
sections.body: Nakavu helps groups of people meet over coffee. We provide it “as is” and keep improving it.

sections.title: Your account
sections.body: Use a real email address you control. You’re responsible for what happens under your account.

sections.title: Behaviour
sections.body: Be kind. Don’t use Nakavu for spam, harassment or sales. Admins can remove members from their workspaces.

sections.title: Workspaces
sections.body: Whoever creates a workspace is responsible for inviting its members and making sure they want to take part.

sections.title: Liability
sections.body: Meetings happen directly between people. Nakavu doesn’t organise them and isn’t responsible for what happens over coffee.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: We may update these terms. We’ll email you in advance about material changes.
